bib.title: BlenderBot 3: a deployed conversational agent that continually learns to responsibly engage

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; appendix F figures are images (example dialogues) not readable as text.

question: How can an open-domain dialogue agent with internet search and long-term memory be built at 175B scale, deployed publicly, and prepared for continual learning from organic user feedback while staying safe?
hypothesis: Deploying a modular, internet-augmented agent to organic users and learning from their feedback (robust to trolls) will yield ever-improving, more responsible dialogue models.
contributions: BB3 model: 175B transformer initialised from OPT-175B, fine-tuned on modular tasks (search decision, query, knowledge, entity, memory, dialogue)
Study of training on human feedback (companion paper Xu et al. 2022b) used to fine-tune on many user-defined tasks
Deployment design incl. UI and initial organic-user experiments
Techniques for robust learning against adversarial users (companion paper Ju et al. 2022)
Overall results: outperforms openly available chatbots incl. predecessors
Release of weights, code, model card, datasets, publications; plan for releasing deployment data

method.summary: A single transformer (3B R2C2 encoder-decoder; 30B and 175B OPT decoder-only) is fine-tuned to execute ten modules selected by control tokens (search decision, query generation, knowledge response, entity extraction, memory generation/access decision/access, dialogue response); modules run in sequence with Mojeek as external search. Models are fine-tuned one epoch on ~4M examples (1.13B tokens) plus pretraining LM data, deployed at blenderbot.ai with a separate safety classifier and canned responses, and evaluated by crowdworkers, organic-user feedback and Safety Bench.

training.objective: supervised sequence-to-sequence fine-tuning on module tasks with control tokens, multitasked with original pre-train LM task and SaFeRDialogues
training.lr: BB3-3B 1e-6 (after warmup); BB3-30B/175B maximum 6e-6 (the LR at end of pre-training)
training.lr_schedule: 3B: linear warmup; 30B/175B: linear warmup then polynomial decay (printed 'polynomial weight decay', decay factor 0.1)
training.epochs: 1 epoch for 30B and 175B (overfit significantly with more)
training.regularisation: multitasking with pretrain LM task; single epoch; early stopping on validation subset for 3B

other.note_batch: Printed '218' and '219' in extracted text, superscripts lost; 2^18 tokens x 5600 updates ~1.5B tokens is consistent with 1.13B+170m only roughly, and 2^19 x 2800 ~1.5B too. Treat as inferred.

inference.decoding: Per module. Decision, query: greedy. BB3-175B dialogue response: factual nucleus sampling; other 175B modules greedy with repetition penalties. BB3-3B: beam search with n-gram blocking.
inference.samples: one generation per item (175B avoids multi-candidate decoding for latency)
inference.prompting: OPT-175B baselines prompted zero-shot and few-shot with in-context examples per module (Table 18)
inference.retrieval: Mojeek search engine returns N documents (N not stated); 'news july 2022' appended to query in current-events eval; memory sampled to fit 2048 tokens for OPT models, Fusion-in-Decoder for 3B

parameters.factual_nucleus: top_p 0.9, lambda-decay 0.9, omega-bound 0.3, p-reset after each full stop
parameters.rep_penalties_175B: alpha_pres = alpha_freq = 0.5 for entity, memory access, knowledge; dialogue also alpha_pres_src = alpha_freq_src = 0.5
parameters.3B_memory_gen: beam 3, min beam length 10, trigram blocking
parameters.3B_entity: beam 3, trigram blocking on output and context
parameters.3B_knowledge: beam 3, min length 10, trigram blocking on output and context
parameters.3B_dialogue: beam 10, min length 20, trigram blocking on output and context

limits: Mistakes include off-topic, nonsensical, incorrect, rude; mitigations trade off with engagingness
Continual learning is in its infancy; the paper does not retrain on deployment data; studies in Sec 5 mostly use crowdworker data
Safety benchmarks are static and crowd-sourced; BB3-175B still toxic in adversarial context (27.8% flagged, higher than BB1 16.1%)
BB3-3B and 175B deployment stats collected at different times, may not be comparable
Prompts for OPT baselines not tuned
Current release uses modular supervision but not DIRECTOR
Nothing on ablation of the modular design vs single-pass; 175B overfit if more than one epoch

terms.definition: learning that continues over time using data from the model's interactions, but training itself will actually be performed in successive large batches; the model is not updated online
